issue.title: Bug: zebra speed timer race sets ACTIVE before RTM_NEWLINK on high-port-count devices

failure.body:
## Description

On high-port-count devices (e.g., 512-port configurations with 362+ routed L3 interfaces), zebra's `if_zebra_speed_update()` timer can fire before RTM_NEWLINK has been processed for all interfaces, causing a race condition that leads to either a crash (SIGABRT) or routing failure on affected interfaces.

### Root Cause

When FRR starts, it reads `zebra.conf` which contains `interface EthernetX` statements for each routed L3 port (generated from CONFIG_DB `INTERFACE` table via `zebra.interfaces.conf.j2`). Each creates an `ifp` with `ifindex = IFINDEX_INTERNAL (0)` and schedules a speed update timer at 15 seconds.

On high-port-count devices, the kernel takes >15 seconds to send `RTM_NEWLINK` for all physical ports (hardware PHY init, ASIC bring-up). When the speed timer fires before `RTM_NEWLINK`:

1. `if_zebra_speed_update()` calls `if_add_update(ifp)` with `ifindex = 0`
2. `if_add_update()` sets `ZEBRA_INTERFACE_ACTIVE` on the interface
3. When `RTM_NEWLINK` finally arrives, the handler sees the interface is already `ACTIVE`
4. It takes **Branch 3** (the "already active" update path) instead of **Branch 1** (the "new interface" path)

### Impact of Branch 3

Branch 3 (`zebra/interface.c`, the update path for already-active interfaces) only calls `if_set_index()` — it does **NOT** call `if_add_update()` / `zebra_ns_link_ifp()`. This means:

- The interface is **never linked into the per-NS ifindex rbtree** (`zebra_ns.ifp_tree`)
- `if_lookup_by_index_per_ns()` returns `NULL` for that interface
- When `RTM_NEWADDR` arrives (IP address assignment), the dplane handler calls `if_lookup_by_index_per_ns()` to find the interface → **returns NULL** → IP address silently dropped
- No connected route installed for that interface
- **BGP sessions cannot form** on affected interfaces
- Nexthop resolution fails → routes blackholed through affected interfaces

The BGP failure itself is observable — monitoring detects sessions down. However, the **root cause is difficult to diagnose**: zebra logs no error, the interface appears UP in `show interface`, and standard recovery (BGP restart) does not resolve it because the rbtree linkage remains broken. Only a full device reboot clears the condition.

### The Existing Guard (Option A) Is Insufficient

The `IFINDEX_INTERNAL` guard in `zebra_ns_link_ifp()` (added in the rbtree rewrite patch, and present in upstream FRR 10.5.1) prevents the crash by returning early when `ifindex == 0`. However, it does **not** prevent:
- The premature `ZEBRA_INTERFACE_ACTIVE` flag being set
- RTM_NEWLINK taking Branch 3 instead of Branch 1
- The interface being missing from the rbtree

Without Option C, the crash is prevented but the routing failure persists — trading a loud, immediately-detected crash for a condition that requires a reboot to resolve and gives no diagnostic clue to the root cause.

### Fix (Option C)

Guard `if_add_update()` in the speed timer to only run when the interface has a valid kernel ifindex:

```c
// zebra/interface.c — if_zebra_speed_update()
if (new_speed != ifp->speed) {
    if_update_state_speed(ifp, new_speed);
-   if_add_update(ifp);
+   if (ifp->ifindex != IFINDEX_INTERNAL)
+       if_add_update(ifp);
    changed = true;
}
```

This ensures the speed timer never sets `ACTIVE` before `RTM_NEWLINK` has assigned a real ifindex. The speed value is still recorded on the interface struct regardless.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a device with 300+ routed L3 interfaces (each with IP in CONFIG_DB `INTERFACE` table)
2. Reboot the device
3. Observe zebra.log — speed timers fire for interfaces that still have `ifindex = IFINDEX_INTERNAL`
4. Check `vtysh -c "show interface json"` — affected interfaces may show `index: 0` or have missing connected routes

The race depends on hardware initialization speed. On 512-port devices with slow PHY init, the window is reliable. On smaller port counts or fast hardware, RTM_NEWLINK may complete before the 15s timer fires.

## Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

**Actual**: On high-port-count devices, zebra either crashes (SIGABRT at `zebra_ns.c` rbtree assertion) or fails to link interfaces into the rbtree, causing BGP/routing failures on affected ports that persist until reboot.

**Expected**: All interfaces should be properly linked in the per-NS ifindex rbtree after boot, regardless of port count or hardware initialization speed.

## Affected Branches

| Branch | Option A (crash guard) | Option C (this fix) needed |
|--------|----------------------|--------------------------|
| master | ✅ In FRR 10.5.1 submodule | ✅ |
| 202505 | ✅ Patch 0060 | ✅ |
| 202511 | ✅ Patch 0062 | ✅ |
| 202411 | ❌ ([PR #24358](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/24358) pending) | ✅ |

## Related

- PR #24311 — Option A guard for master (merged Oct 2025)
- PR #24358 — Option A backport to 202411 (pending, 5 months stalled)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <<EMAIL>>

## FRR Upstream

- **FRR Issue**: [FRRouting/frr#19792](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/issues/19792) — same bug, filed by Arista
- **[FRR PR #19794](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/19794)** (merged) — Option A: guard in `zebra_ns_link_ifp()` (crash prevention only)
- **[FRR PR #19804](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/19804)** (open, by mjstapp) — Complete upstream fix: moves speed timer from `if_zebra_new_hook()` to `zebra_if_dplane_ifp_handling()` (only after RTM_NEWLINK), adds `IFINDEX_INTERNAL` guard in `if_add_update()`. This eliminates the race entirely. Our Option C patch is the interim SONiC fix until FRR upgrades to a version containing [FRRouting/frr#19804](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/19804).

---

### Fix Tracking

| Target | PR | Status |
|--------|-----|--------|
| **master** | #26458 | ✅ Merged (2026-04-07) |
| **202505** | TBD | TODO |
| **202511** | #26630 | Merged |
| **202411** | — | ⏸️ Blocked on [PR #24358](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/24358) (Option A prerequisite, stalled 5 months) |
| **sonic-mgmt** | sonic-net/sonic-mgmt#23406 | Open |
| **FRR upstream** | [FRRouting/frr#19804](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/19804) | Open (complete fix by mjstapp) |

resolution.title: [SONiC-only] zebra: skip if_add_update in speed timer for unready interfaces
resolution.description:
> **Note:** This is a SONiC-only interim patch. The upstream FRR PR ([FRRouting/frr#19804](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/19804)) redesigns the speed timer to only start after RTM_NEWLINK, eliminating the race entirely. Once that lands in the FRR version used by SONiC, this patch should be removed.

#### Why I did it

Fixes #26457

On high-port-count devices (512+ ports with 362+ routed L3 interfaces), the `if_zebra_speed_update()` timer fires before `RTM_NEWLINK` assigns a real ifindex. This calls `if_add_update()` with `ifindex = IFINDEX_INTERNAL (0)`, which sets `ZEBRA_INTERFACE_ACTIVE` prematurely.

When `RTM_NEWLINK` later arrives, it sees the interface is already ACTIVE and takes the update branch (Branch 3) instead of the new-interface branch (Branch 1). Branch 3 only calls `if_set_index()` — it does **not** call `zebra_ns_link_ifp()`, so the interface is never linked into the per-NS ifindex rbtree. This causes:

- `if_lookup_by_index_per_ns()` returns NULL for affected interfaces
- `RTM_NEWADDR` silently dropped → no connected route installed
- BGP sessions cannot form on affected ports
- Nexthops blackholed silently

The existing `IFINDEX_INTERNAL` guard in `zebra_ns_link_ifp()` (Option A, already present in master via FRR 10.5.1) prevents the crash but does **not** prevent the silent routing failure.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO: 37114309

#### How I did it

Added a guard in `if_zebra_speed_update()` to skip the `if_add_update()` call when `ifp->ifindex == IFINDEX_INTERNAL`. The speed value is still recorded on the interface struct regardless.

```diff
 if (new_speed != ifp->speed) {
     if_update_state_speed(ifp, new_speed);
-    if_add_update(ifp);
+    if (ifp->ifindex != IFINDEX_INTERNAL)
+        if_add_update(ifp);
     changed = true;
 }
```

This ensures the speed timer never sets ACTIVE before RTM_NEWLINK has assigned a real ifindex, so RTM_NEWLINK always takes Branch 1 (new interface path) which properly calls `zebra_ns_link_ifp()`.

Files changed:
- `src/sonic-frr/patch/0065-SONiC-ONLY-zebra-skip-if-add-update-in-speed-timer-for-unready-ifp.patch` (new)
- `src/sonic-frr/patch/series` (added entry)

#### How to verify it

1. Build VS image and deploy on a T0 KVM testbed
2. Verify all interfaces have valid ifindex: `docker exec bgp vtysh -c "show interface json"` — all `index` fields should be > 0
3. Run `config reload` and re-verify
4. Verification test: [sonic-mgmt PR (pending)](https://github.com/deepak-singhal0408/sonic-mgmt/tree/fix/zebra-interface-consistency-test)

**Test results (VS KVM T0 testbed, image `SONiC.fix_zebra-speed-timer-race.0-3fb1b60fa`):**
- ✅ `test_interface_ifindex_after_boot` — 32/32 interfaces valid ifindex
- ✅ `test_interface_ifindex_after_config_reload` — 32/32 interfaces valid after reload

#### Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)

Speed timer race affects all branches that have the rbtree rewrite patch (0062). On 202411, this fix also requires Option A (PR #24358, pending).

- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [x] 202411
- [x] 202505
- [x] 202511

#### Tested branch (Please provide the tested image version)

- [x] SONiC.fix_zebra-speed-timer-race.0-3fb1b60fa (master + this patch, FRR 10.5.1)

#### FRR Upstream

This is an interim SONiC fix. The complete upstream solution is [FRRouting/frr#19804](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/19804) (by mjstapp), which redesigns the speed timer to only start after RTM_NEWLINK, eliminating the race entirely. Our Option C patch will be superseded when SONiC upgrades FRR to a version containing that fix.

Related: [FRRouting/frr#19792](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/issues/19792) (original bug report), [FRRouting/frr#19794](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/19794) (Option A — crash guard only, merged).

#### Description for the changelog

Guard if_add_update() in zebra speed timer to prevent silent routing failure when ifindex is not yet assigned on high-port-count devices.

#### Link to config_db schema for YANG module changes

N/A — no config_db or YANG changes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <<EMAIL>>
